questions.question: How do you set up Sidekiq in a Rails app?
questions.title: Sidekiq Setup Basics
questions.direct_answer: Setup: (1) gem 'sidekiq' in Gemfile, bundle install. (2) Set the adapter: config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq (or use Sidekiq directly: include Sidekiq::Job). (3) Configure Sidekiq: config/initializers/sidekiq.rb with Sidekiq.configure_server / configure_client (Redis URL, logging). (4) Run workers: `bundle exec sidekiq` (reads config/sidekiq.yml for queues, concurrency). (5) (Optional) Mount the Web UI: `require 'sidekiq/web'; mount Sidekiq::Web => '/sidekiq'` in routes (protect with auth in prod). Redis is required (the queue store). Concurrency (threads per process) is set in sidekiq.yml (default 5-10). Queues: sidekiq.yml lists queues with priorities. For prod, run multiple Sidekiq processes behind a process manager (systemd, Upstart). Keep jobs small and idempotent; pass IDs not objects.

sections.title: Sidekiq setup
sections.content:
```ruby
# 1) Gemfile
gem 'sidekiq'
# then: bundle install

# 2) Set the Active Job adapter (config/environments/production.rb)
config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq

#    OR use Sidekiq directly:
class MailJob
  include Sidekiq::Job              # (older: include Sidekiq::Worker)
  def perform(user_id); User.find(user_id); end
end
MailJob.perform_async(1)

# 3) config/initializers/sidekiq.rb (Redis + logging)
Sidekiq.configure_server do |c|
  c.redis = { url: ENV['REDIS_URL'] || 'redis://localhost:6379/0' }
end
Sidekiq.configure_client do |c|
  c.redis = { url: ENV['REDIS_URL'] || 'redis://localhost:6379/0' }
end

# 4) config/sidekiq.yml (queues + concurrency)
#:concurrency: 10
#:queues:
#  - [default, 1]
#  - [mailers, 2]
#  - [urgent, 3]

# Run workers:  bundle exec sidekiq

# 5) Web UI (config/routes.rb) -- PROTECT in production!
# require 'sidekiq/web'
# authenticate :admin do
#   mount Sidekiq::Web => '/sidekiq'
# end

# Redis is REQUIRED (the queue store). Concurrency = threads per process.
# In prod: run multiple Sidekiq processes (systemd/Upstart), each with N threads.
# Keep jobs SMALL and IDEMPOTENT; pass IDs, not objects (JSON-serialized).
```

sections.content:
Setup: (1) gem 'sidekiq' in Gemfile, bundle install. (2) Set the adapter: config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq (or use Sidekiq directly: include Sidekiq::Job). (3) Configure Sidekiq: config/initializers/sidekiq.rb with Sidekiq.configure_server / configure_client (Redis URL, logging). (4) Run workers: `bundle exec sidekiq` (reads config/sidekiq.yml for queues, concurrency). (5) (Optional) Mount the Web UI: `require 'sidekiq/web'; mount Sidekiq::Web => '/sidekiq'` in routes (protect with auth in prod).

Redis is required (the queue store).

Concurrency (threads per process) is set in sidekiq.yml (default 5-10). Queues: sidekiq.yml lists queues with priorities. For prod, run multiple Sidekiq processes behind a process manager (systemd, Upstart). Keep jobs small and idempotent; pass IDs not objects.

Exposing the Sidekiq Web UI without auth in production (anyone could retry/kill jobs).

sections.title: Sidekiq setup
sections.content:
```ruby
# 1) Gemfile
gem 'sidekiq'
# then: bundle install

# 2) Set the Active Job adapter (config/environments/production.rb)
config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq

#    OR use Sidekiq directly:
class MailJob
  include Sidekiq::Job              # (older: include Sidekiq::Worker)
  def perform(user_id); User.find(user_id); end
end
MailJob.perform_async(1)

# 3) config/initializers/sidekiq.rb (Redis + logging)
Sidekiq.configure_server do |c|
  c.redis = { url: ENV['REDIS_URL'] || 'redis://localhost:6379/0' }
end
Sidekiq.configure_client do |c|
  c.redis = { url: ENV['REDIS_URL'] || 'redis://localhost:6379/0' }
end

# 4) config/sidekiq.yml (queues + concurrency)
#:concurrency: 10
#:queues:
#  - [default, 1]
#  - [mailers, 2]
#  - [urgent, 3]

# Run workers:  bundle exec sidekiq

# 5) Web UI (config/routes.rb) -- PROTECT in production!
# require 'sidekiq/web'
# authenticate :admin do
#   mount Sidekiq::Web => '/sidekiq'
# end

# Redis is REQUIRED (the queue store). Concurrency = threads per process.
# In prod: run multiple Sidekiq processes (systemd/Upstart), each with N threads.
# Keep jobs SMALL and IDEMPOTENT; pass IDs, not objects (JSON-serialized).
```
